title: Take an idea to proof
trigger: The Owner decides the product must let an actor do something new.
result: The Owner merges the new behavior, every test of its use case passes, and coverage shows it proved.
notes: Where the spec is the source and Agents are held to it (LA-BO06). The Owner decides the behavior once, as records; the Agent builds from those records, not from the chat that hands them over; a wrong write is refused with its reasons; and the check catches what is left before the Owner reviews. LA-BO09 times this journey, from the use case's first commit to its tests automated; LA-BO06 counts its merges that needed no send-back, and LA-BO08 the mistakes that got past it. The path sent back is taken at the Owner's trace (step 8) when a requirement is not built or proved as meant, and goes back to the Owner's review of the problems (step 7). The Owner hands the work over by asking Claude in the chat (LA-PLT-UC19): by the use-case line (LA-STD-MODELING-R15) that is the chat's goal with another message, not a goal of its own.

title: Bring a product onto Lathe
trigger: A team decides to specify a product it already has in code with Lathe.
result: The product checks clean, with its outcomes, domains and use cases written over the code it has, and the Owner sees what is built, proved and missing.
notes: LA-BO05 counts the products that adopt Lathe; this journey is how each one does, untimed. The product already has code, so the Agent writes the use cases and commands that code carries out, and the check and coverage show what the code builds and what it does not yet prove.

title: Move a product to a new Lathe
result: The product checks clean on the new Lathe, and the Owner has seen everything the move changed.
notes: LA-BO05 counts the products that keep using Lathe; this journey is how each keeps up with it, untimed. The path to-dos left follows the move when it lists work to do by hand, in place of the main path's check.

title: Change something on purpose
trigger: The Owner decides a part of the product must change.
result: The Owner keeps the change, and it moved nothing but what they chose it to touch.
notes: A break is never an accident here: the Owner sees what a change would touch before it is made (LA-TRC-UC24), and any break is one they chose. LA-BO11 counts this journey's breaks the Owner did not see beforehand, and its questions of what a change touches; LA-BO06 counts the changes kept without a send-back, and LA-BO08 the mistakes that got past it. The path touches more than meant is taken after step 2 and goes on to step 3. The path sent back takes the place of step 7 and goes back to step 4. The Owner undoes the turn (LA-PLT-UC27), then tells the Agent why in the chat (LA-PLT-UC19): by the use-case line (LA-STD-MODELING-R15) a send-back is the chat's goal with another message, not a goal of its own.

title: Answer why something exists
trigger: The Owner or a Reader meets a part of the product, such as a screen, a button or a component, and asks why it is there.
result: They can say which requirement, use case and business outcome it exists for and what proves it, or the Owner has removed a part that serves nothing.
notes: LA-BO11 counts the why questions this journey answers from Lathe alone, and their minutes; LA-BO10 times it for someone new, at a desk and on a phone, where the same steps run and the phone only changes the layout. The main path is one sitting of one actor, a duration a use case could time (the discover-outcomes rule); it stays a journey because the path serves nothing hands the decision to an Agent. That path is taken at step 3, when no outcome reaches the part.

title: See where the product stands
trigger: The Owner needs to know where the product stands, such as before choosing the next work.
result: The Owner knows what is built, proved and missing, and has handed the weakest part to an Agent as the next work.
notes: LA-BO07 counts what this journey leaves unanswered: each status question the Owner still asks an Agent, and each coverage claim found false on the path a claim found false. That path is taken at any step when a claim looks wrong, and goes on to step 5 with the false claim as the next work.
